## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bakajātaka* (Ja 405, also cited as the *Brahmā Baka Jātaka*) is a canonical birth-story preserved in the Jātaka collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [Bodhi 2003]. According to the traditional introductory setting, the Buddha recounted this tale while residing at Jetavana concerning the deity Baka Brahmā. The name *Baka* literally translates to "crane," a bird traditionally regarded in Indian folklore as an archetype of deceit and cunning [Bodhi 2003].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: SN 6.4 Bakabrahmasutta

- [Bodhi 2003] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Connected Discourses of the Buddha: A New Translation of the Saṁyutta Nikāya (2003) — Identifies Ja 405 as the Brahmā Baka Jātaka, notes the meaning of the name Baka, and explains its equivalence to SN 6.4 and thematic link to MN 49.
